key_insight: A robotic, AI-guided cold gas-dynamic spraying workflow can reclaim and protect steel marine propellers on-site while avoiding thermal distortion and improving coating durability.
engineering_relevance: The study proposes a practical end-to-end repair cell for large marine propellers that combines defect mapping, surface preparation, coating deposition, and force-controlled finishing in one automated system.
method: 6-axis robot with AI/computer-vision for contactless 3D defect mapping
Supersonic cold gas-dynamic spraying via automatic tool changer
Force-Torque adaptive finish grinding after coating
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an estimated 4–5× increase in protective coating service life versus conventional methods and evaluates economic viability for on-site repair of supertankers.
watch_item: Industrial deployment will depend on reliable vision/force calibration and robust operation under variable blade geometry, surface damage, and shipyard conditions.
paper_title: Automated Complex for the Reclamation and Anti-Corrosion Protection of Steel Marine Propellers via Supersonic Cold Gas-Dynamic Spraying Utilizing AI-Driven Control
